documents.title: SQuAD: 100,000+ Questions for Machine Comprehension of Text

chunks.text: The original SQuAD benchmark contains 107,785 question-answer pairs drawn from 536 Wikipedia articles. The evaluation is limited to answers that can be selected as spans in the supplied passage, which makes scoring simpler than for free-form answers.

In the original SQuAD v1.0 human evaluation, the second answer served as a prediction and the other answers as references. On the test split, human exact match was 77.0% and the human F1 score was 86.8%.

documents.title: Know What You Don’t Know: Unanswerable Questions for SQuAD

chunks.text: SQuAD 2.0 extends the previous SQuAD dataset with more than 50,000 difficult unanswerable questions. Crowdworkers wrote questions that look answerable in context. Systems must abstain if a paragraph does not support an answer.

For SQuAD 2.0, the DocQA + ELMo F1 score was 67.6% on the development split. The F1 score was 66.3% on the test split. The same architecture trained on the original SQuAD obtained a test F1 score of 85.8%. Human test F1 on SQuAD 2.0 was 89.5%.

SQuAD 2.0 human evaluation pooled crowdworker responses by majority vote, with an average of 4.8 responses per question. The authors point out that the original SQuAD evaluation used a single person's prediction, which may have underestimated human accuracy.

documents.title: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers for Language Understanding

chunks.text: On SQuAD 2.0, BERT Large (single model) obtained a test F1 score of 83.1% and test exact match of 80.0%. On the development split it obtained an F1 score of 81.9%.

For SQuAD 2.0 the authors tuned the abstention threshold on the development split to maximize F1. BERT was fine-tuned for 2 epochs with a learning rate of 5e-5 and a batch size of 48. The SQuAD 2.0 model did not use TriviaQA.

On SQuAD 1.1, the BERT Large ensemble with TriviaQA obtained a test F1 score of 93.2%. A single BERT Large model with TriviaQA scored 91.8% F1 on the test split. The ensemble combined seven systems that used different checkpoints and fine-tuning seeds.
